source.title: Look Before You Leap: Enhancing Attention and Vigilance Regarding Harmful Content with GuidelineLLM
source.authors: Shao-Qing Zhang; Zhuo-Sheng Zhang; Ke-Hai Chen; Rong-Xiang Weng; Mu-Yun Yang; Tie-Jun Zhao; Min Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates how often jailbreak prompts produce harmful responses from chat models, using ASR rather than the original studies' fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: Rows record the reported No Defense attack-success results. The study also reports ASR for several defense methods, but those comparisons concern the performance of the defenses rather than an additional test of the claim that attacks bypass refusal. It does not test fine-tuning the responding models, compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, per-token KL, or safety localization.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper. The No Defense ASRs in Tables 2 and 7 are baselines for GuidelineLLM, not a test of any version. The attacks are whole jailbreak prompts (DAN, role play, AutoDAN templates, GPT-generated T-Jailbreak). None isolates a compliant-opening prefill, an adversarial suffix or a decoding change, so V4 is not tested. The study does no fine-tuning of the responding models, KL analysis, localization or deepening, and cites Qi et al. only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: GuidelineLLM, a fine-tuned model that feeds risk guidelines to the responding LLM, cuts ASR by 34.17% on average while keeping helpfulness, without safety-tuning the responding models.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests inference-time jailbreak prompts and a guideline-based defense; it does not use the original studies' fine-tuning safety intervention or token-position KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by responding model, jailbreak dataset, and T-Jailbreak technique. The number of guidelines also affects ASR in the defense experiments, but those results are not rows for this claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Undefended Llama2-7B-Chat resists most in-the-wild jailbreak prompts: ASR 0-9.5% on DAN, SAP200 and JailbreakChatGPT. AutoDAN reaches 58.57%. Vicuna models show 33-97% ASR. All scored by refusal-token detection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic jailbreak prompts (persona, template, optimized prompt) bypass refusal in safety-tuned chat models at rates depending on model alignment strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Role-play and logical-reasoning templates reach 63-80% ASR on 30 questions each, even on Llama2-7B-Chat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak technique type modulates bypass rates in safety-tuned chat models.

record.problems: The paper uses rule-based detection for ASR; it notes that safe responses can be counted as successful attacks by token-based detection. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The technique-level results shown here cover only three of the seven summarized techniques.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining Table 2 defense-method ASRs and Table 7 Self-Reminder ASRs were left out because they report performance of the study's defense comparisons, rather than an additional No Defense test of jailbreak bypass. Table 3 judges examples under GuidelineLLM only and does not add a No Defense attack result.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of responding models.
No benign fine-tuning of responding models.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks isolated; only whole jailbreak prompts.
No analysis of causes of shallowness.
No deepening training of the responding models; the defense is prompt-side guidelines.

record.verdict_notes: The ASR measure is rule-based refusal-token detection. Table 3 shows many responses counted as successful attacks are judged harmless by GPT-3.5, so ASR likely overstates harm. Table 7 shows only 3 of the 7 techniques despite its caption. Peer-reviewed at AAAI 2025 per the copyright line, though the record says preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on safety.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
The study tests jailbreak prompts broadly, including AutoDAN and named jailbreak techniques. It does not isolate compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, or a specific suffix intervention.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether that effect holds.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: No Defense on AutoDAN for all three responding models; and on DAN, SAP200, JailbreakChatGPT, and T-Jailbreak for Vicuna-7B and Vicuna-13B
reader_labels.reason: The reported ASRs show jailbreak prompts eliciting harmful responses, with rates including 90.77% and 96.92% on AutoDAN; see r4, r6-r15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Attack success varies substantially by model, dataset, and T-Jailbreak technique
reader_labels.reason: Some combinations have low or zero ASR, including 0.00 on JailbreakChatGPT for Llama2-7B-Chat and 1.62 on SAP200; see r2-r3 and r19-r24.
